text:
incident-bot: PAGE: Dedicated pool observability gap for CascadeBank (vpc-prod-dedicated-7). Missing spans and delayed logs seen since ~02:10 UTC. Paging SRE oncall. :rotating_light:
Devon (oncall): I’m on it. setting priority P1 for now. any customer-visible errors reported?
CS Liaison: CascadeBank reports slow support traces in their console and says their alerting fired. They can see some metrics but many traces are missing and logs show 403 when they try to fetch tenant keys.
Marina Li: Is this the same forwarder mismatch from the recent config roll? last week we saw per-tenant forwarder routing flip for a subset of vpc tenants.
Kai Thompson: Checking forwarder logs... I see spikes and a signature mismatch from proxy side for tenant ID cb-428. Looks like our routing header (x-tenant-origin) was rewritten to a different shard.
Sam Patel: Confirming. The vpc-forwarder (fw-7) had a segfault restarts around 02:08 and came back with old env var set (LEGACY_SHARD=true). That would cause mismatched stitching in traces.
Devon (oncall): Good catch. Are spans lost or just not stitched/attributed?
Marina Li: Instrumentation shows spans were emitted from model workers but the trace IDs never reached the trace aggregator for cb-428. Logs inbound to forwarder show 200, but aggregator rejects due to tenant header mismatch, returns 403.
CS Liaison: CascadeBank is asking for an ETA to see traces restored. Also asking if any data needs re-ingest.
Kai Thompson: Immediate mitigation: re-route cb-428 traffic to backup forwarder (fw-3) which has correct env. That will restore live stitching. I'll patch routing rule now.
Devon (oncall): +1 do it. Also need a temporary customer message to explain limited access and that we’re working on restoring full trace view. Sam, you handle postmortem for the segfault gap.
Sam Patel: Copy. I’ll pull core dumps and trace the restart cause. Tagging it as fw-7 crash -> env drift.
Marina Li: While Kai switches route, we should open a read-only shadow bridge so CascadeBank can view past spans (if we can replay). We may need to pull from the worker buffer; retention window is 6h.
Infra Proxy: Re-route applied: cb-428 -> fw-3. I’m watching for handshake success. Backend reports: handshake ok, trace aggregator returning 202 for new spans.
CS Liaison: CascadeBank notified: "We’re routing your telemetry to a stable forwarder. You may see restored traces within a few minutes. We’re still investigating a small window of missing spans around 02:06–02:09 UTC."
Devon (oncall): Can someone confirm logs access? The customer also said they can’t fetch tenant logs via the VPC api (403). Is that the same auth shard issue?
Kai Thompson: Yes, the log-access service also validates x-tenant-origin against shard map. Because fw-7 restarted with LEGACY_SHARD=true, it sent a header the log service didn't recognize. fw-3 uses the correct header so it should restore log reads.
Sam Patel: I see reads succeeding for new requests. For the failed window, we can run a selective re-ingest: fetch from worker local buffer and push to aggregator with corrected tenant header. I can kick that off if we approve. It will backfill spans and logs into the aggregated traces.
Marina Li: Backfill plan: target only cb-428, 02:05–02:12 UTC. Steps: (1) export buffered payloads from worker nodes, (2) scrub/validate, (3) re-post to aggregator with correct headers via staging endpoint. This will take ~30–45m depending on buffer size.
Devon (oncall): Approved. Coordinate with CS for a customer-facing ETA, and with infra for backend rate limits. Also add a temporary audit log entry to show we modified routing for this tenant.
CS Liaison: Notified CascadeBank that we’re backfilling and expect to restore missing spans/logs within 45 minutes. They want a brief confirmation when backfill completes.
Infra Proxy: Rate limit note: re-ingest will bump token usage on aggregator. I've increased burst quota for cb-428 for 1h to prevent throttles.
Kai Thompson: Starting export from worker buffer. Command I ran:
```
ssh worker-23
jq '.payloads[] | select(.tenant=="cb-428" and .ts>=16200 and .ts<=16332)' buffer.json > cb428-window.json
```
Sam Patel: I’ll validate payloads and run dedupe pass. Running small test post to staging aggregator now.
Marina Li: Heads up — we need to scrub any PII before re-posting. CS confirmed CascadeBank permits re-ingest under their contract, but we must run the scrub pipeline.
Sam Patel: scrub pipeline ran. Test post to staging returned 202 and shows traces stitched. Initiating bulk re-post now.
Devon (oncall): Keep logs of each step. Notify security/compliance that we performed backfill under customer authorization.
CS Liaison: CascadeBank responding: "Thanks — we see partial traces coming in now. We'll wait for full backfill and will confirm when everything looks reconciled."
Infra Proxy: Bulk re-post is in progress. 12% complete. No errors so far. Throttles are within adjusted quota.
Kai Thompson: Monitoring aggregator: p95 trace latency unchanged, no error spikes. Forwarder health: fw-3 stable.
Devon (oncall): Any sign of persistent config drift that caused fw-7 to restart into legacy?
Sam Patel: fw-7 core dump indicates an NPE in config reload path during env var parsing. I’ll open a bug and ping runtime team; this looks like a regression introduced in the last env-parsing change.
Marina Li: For immediate prevention, add a preflight check on forwarder start that validates shard mapping vs config. We'll push hotfix to image build after incident.
CS Liaison: CascadeBank: "We appreciate the rapid response. Please notify us when the backfill finishes and share a short summary of root cause and next steps."
Infra Proxy: Re-post complete. All buffered payloads for cb-428 in target window have been accepted.
Sam Patel: Verification: aggregator shows traces for 02:05–02:12 UTC for cb-428. Cross-checked with customer sample IDs — matches.
Devon (oncall): Excellent. Mark incident mitigated for customer impact. Actions:
- Short-term: route cb tenants off fw-7 until fw-7 image hotfix is deployed.
- Mid-term: add preflight env validation on forwarder start.
- Postmortem: root cause fw-7 env-parsing NPE, release regression.
CS Liaison: Sending final note to CascadeBank with summary and timeline.
Marina Li: I’ll file the postmortem and include steps to harden forwarder start path and add integration test for shard mapping.
Devon (oncall): Closing on-call handoff in 30m. If anything regresses, page SRE again. Great job everyone. :tada:
